supporting_observations.claim: Lena Ward's workstation launched mstsc to DC-SUN-01 and initiated a TCP connection to its RDP port shortly before the alerted account-creation time; these records do not establish that an RDP logon succeeded.

At 14:11 UTC, Lena Ward's workstation launched dsa.msc with a high-integrity token and MMC made LDAP and RPC-related connections to DC-SUN-01. This is consistent with directory administration, but does not show which directory operation occurred.

The inventory says Lena Ward can create domain accounts, and that help-desk temporary accounts use the v.<name> format and are added only to Vendors. That makes the alert's stated account name compatible with an authorized workflow, but the logs provided do not verify the account's creation details or group membership.

The inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-IDOYLE-01, whereas the observed RDP attempt to DC-SUN-01 originated from WS-LWARD-01. This is a policy discrepancy requiring clarification, but does not by itself establish malicious account creation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records contain no domain-controller account-creation audit event or other direct record confirming creation of v.rwong.
The supplied records do not show whether the RDP connection resulted in an authenticated session.
The supplied records show directory-management tooling and network connections, but not the specific directory objects or changes made.
No records show the new account's group memberships, privileges, creator, or subsequent use.
claims_not_established: That v.rwong was actually created at the stated time, or who created it.
That the account was placed only in the Vendors group or was granted additional privileges.
That Lena Ward's RDP connection to DC-SUN-01 succeeded or was authorized.
That the directory activity at 14:11 UTC was the creation or modification of v.rwong.
additional_evidence_needed: Domain-controller security audit events around 13:20–14:20 UTC, especially account creation and group-membership or privilege changes, with subject and target account details.
DC-SUN-01 logon and RDP session records to determine whether Lena Ward authenticated and what session or account performed any changes.
Directory audit or change-history data for v.rwong, including creation time, creator, enabled state, group memberships, and assigned privileges.
The help-desk request or change record authorizing the temporary account, if one exists.
unrelated_findings: Chrome was launched to console.aws.amazon.com from WS-LWARD-01; AWS is not among the approved services in the supplied inventory. This does not establish use of an unapproved storage service and does not decide the account alert. (T238-00019, T238-00023, T238-00025)
The proxy recorded a POST to api.pagerduty.com from WS-LWARD-01, a service not listed among the approved services in the supplied inventory. This is separate from the account alert. (T238-00024)
